XVII.}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=17|verse=1}}}}ND vvhen they had vvalked through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to The{{ls}}salonica, vvhere there vvas a {{ls}}ynagogue of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=2}}† And Paul according to his cu{{ls}}tome entred in vnto them, & three Sabboths he di{{ls}}cour{{ls}}ed to them out of the Scriptures, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=3}}† declaring and in{{ls}}inuating that it behoued {{sc|Christ}} to {{ls}}uffer and to ri{{ls}}e againe from the dead: and that this is {{sc|Iesvs Christ}}, vvhom I preach to you. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=4}}† And certaine of them beleeued, and vvere ioyned to Paul and Silas, and of the Gentiles that {{ls}}erued God a great multitude, and noble vvomen not a fevv. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=5}}† But the Ievves {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Zelantes''. This is the zeale of Heretikes, and a liuely paterne of their dealing at this day again{{ls}}t Catholike Prie{{ls}}ts and preachers and the good ''Ia{{ls}}ons'' that receiue them.}}∷ enuying, & taking vnto them of the ra{{ls}}cal {{ls}}ort certaine naughtie men, and making a tumult, {{ls}}tirred the citie: and be{{ls}}etting Ia{{ls}}ons hou{{ls}}e, {{ls}}ought to bring them forth vnto the people. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=6}}† And not finding them, they drevv Ia{{ls}}on and certaine brethren to the princes of the citie, crying, That the{{ls}}e are they that {{ls}}tirre vp the vvorld, and are come hither, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=7}}† vvhom Ia{{ls}}on hath receiued, and al the{{ls}}e doe again{{ls}}t the decrees of Cæ{{ls}}ar, {{ls}}aying that there is an other king, {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=8}}† And they moued the people, and the princes of the citie hearing the{{ls}}e things. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=9}}† And taking a {{ls}}atisfaction of Ia{{ls}}on and of the re{{ls}}t, they dimi{{ls}}sed them. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=10}}† But the brethren forthwith by night {{ls}}ent away Paul and Silas vnto Berœa.

Vvho vvhen they vvere come, entred into the {{ls}}ynagogue of the Iewes. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=11}}† (And the{{ls}}e were more noble then they that are at The{{ls}}salonica, vvho receiued the vvord vvith al greedines, daily {{sup|‖}} {{ls}}earching the {{ls}}criptures, if the{{ls}}e things vvere {{ls}}o. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=12}}† And many {{ls}}urely of them beleeued, and of hone{{ls}}t women Gentiles, and men not a few.) {{verse|chapter=17|verse=13}}† And vvhen the Iewes in The{{ls}}salonica vnder{{ls}}tood, that at Berœa al{{ls}}o the vvord of God was preached by Paul, they came thither al{{ls}}o, mouing and troubling the multitude. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=14}}† And then immediatly the<noinclude>{{rh|||brethren}}</noinclude>
